audit_findings.title: Parent-share denominator may be paired with consolidated-basis owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: A hybrid owner-earnings numerator would combine parent-attributable income with consolidated Egypt add-backs, capital spending, working-capital movements, or cash before dividing by APA parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Sinopec International Petroleum Exploration and Production Corporation (Sinopec) owns a one-third minority participation in the Company’s consolidated Egypt oil and gas business as a noncontrolling interest, which is reflected as a separate noncontrolling interest component of equity in the Company’s consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The one-third Egypt noncontrolling interest is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not reconcile the $946.9 million anchor sufficiently to demonstrate the net numerator error or its direction. The exposure is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: 2025 noncontrolling-interest income was $258 million, distributions were $430 million, and its filed standardized discounted cash flows were about $1.0 billion, versus the $13.748 billion base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every 2025 owner-earnings component on an APA-parent basis, including Egypt D&A, noncash charges, capital expenditures, working capital, retirement spending, taxes, distributions, and the portion of bridge cash legally attributable to Sinopec; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Legacy Gulf decommissioning is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $806 million net recorded claim at 2026-06-30 ($847 million liability less $41 million security asset), equal to $2.26 per diluted share and 5.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Future decommissioning cash payments reduce owner earnings or require a separate negative equity-bridge adjustment; they are not represented by interest expense on financial debt.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, Apache estimates that its potential liability to fund the remaining decommissioning of Legacy GOA Assets and assets previously sold to other operators ranges from $ 0.9 billion to $ 1.2 billion on an undiscounted basis.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission from the stated bridge, which contains cash but no Gulf decommissioning adjustment. The net recorded claim exceeds the $444 million cash balance and is large enough to reduce the $45.29 bull value to approximately $43.03 per share if treated as a direct adjustment, close to the $42.77 market price. The final economic adjustment may differ because payment timing must be discounted.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest payment schedule, trust and security balances, reimbursements, tax effects, and amounts already reflected in owner earnings; deduct the resulting net present cash burden once and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The $2.88 billion ARO requires explicit cash-flow treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.930 billion recorded ARO at 2026-06-30, equal to $8.22 per diluted share and 21.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Actual plugging, removal, and restoration payments must reduce forecast owner earnings when paid or be recognized once in the equity bridge; adding back accretion and depreciation without those payments inflates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the asset retirement obligation (ARO) balance totaled $ 2,880 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its scale are demonstrated, but the supplied owner-earnings reconciliation does not establish how much settlement cash is already embedded in the $946.9 million anchor or future maintenance capital. Because the recorded ARO is more than three times annual anchor owner earnings, omission could plainly change the valuation conclusion. The full accounting balance cannot automatically be deducted because timing, recoveries, taxes, and overlap with forecast capital and the North Sea finding must be reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an asset-level ARO payment schedule using the latest $2.930 billion liability, partner recoveries, tax effects, and currency assumptions; map payments into forecast owner earnings and rerun, with an explicit control preventing bridge or North Sea double counting.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain large nonrecurring gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $508 million of identified gains ($301 million divestiture, $147 million debt extinguishment, and $60 million Gulf remeasurement), equal to 53.6% of the $946.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained nonrecurring gain increases anchor owner earnings and is then compounded through explicit growth and the terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognized a gain of $ 299 million in association with this sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are filed and unquestionably material relative to the anchor, but their inclusion in owner earnings is unresolved because the complete reconciliation was not supplied. Thus this is not yet a demonstrated anchor error. The filed $77 million unrealized derivative loss also requires separate normalization, but it does not reduce the materiality of the possible retained gains.
audit_findings.action: Produce an auditable reconciliation from $1.434 billion parent-attributable income to the $946.9 million anchor, showing removal of each divestiture, debt-extinguishment, Gulf remeasurement, and unrealized derivative item while retaining recurring costs; correct any retained item and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A known North Sea exit contradicts a null perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 North Sea standardized discounted future net cash flows were negative $869 million, equal to $2.44 per diluted share and 6.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The null perimeter applies consolidated growth and terminal value to earnings from operations scheduled to cease before 2030, while potentially omitting runoff, cessation taxes, and decommissioning cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company determined that expected returns did not economically support making investments required under the combined impact of the regulations and expects to cease production at its facilities in the North Sea prior to 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: The cessation plan and the model's null perimeter are both demonstrated. Although North Sea generated only $21 million of 2025 segment operating income, its filed standardized value was negative because future development and decommissioning costs outweighed inflows. The $869 million scale could reduce the $45.29 bull value to about $42.85 per share, essentially the $42.77 market price, although that standardized measure is not itself a direct DCF adjustment and overlaps the ARO finding.
audit_findings.action: Replace uniform growth for North Sea with a production, revenue, operating-cost, tax, and decommissioning runoff through cessation; remove it from terminal value and rerun all scenarios while reconciling all ARO amounts to avoid duplication.

audit_findings.title: Suriname growth spending and future production may be mismatched
audit_findings.magnitude: $256 million of 2025 development and facility capital, equal to 27.0% of anchor owner earnings; filed 2025 standardized discounted value was $636 million, or $1.78 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Treating pre-production development spending as recurring maintenance depresses anchor owner earnings, while excluding it without forecasting remaining funding and attributable production overstates value; both sides affect growth and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, the Company spent approximately $ 256 million in development and facility capital as part of the Suriname development during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The current spending and future production project are demonstrated, but the supplied reconciliation and null perimeter do not show whether either side is represented consistently. The spending is large relative to the anchor, and the project's filed standardized value is material relative to the narrow differences among market price and scenario values, so the mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion despite its unresolved direction.
audit_findings.action: Separate Suriname growth capital from maintenance capital; forecast APA's carried and uncarrried funding obligations, first-oil timing, ownership after Staatsolie participation, operating costs, taxes, royalties, and attributable post-2028 cash flows; then rerun all scenarios on one consistent ownership basis.
